title: The swarm lab's Pearl mode: the game's Pearl bodies down the canyon's lane at the game's camera height, a step and a draw reading, nine live knobs and a sweep into a table (owner, 2026-10-14: measure first, then the level ladder)
context: Owner, 2026-10-14: 'brainstorm possibilities to show more pearl-enemies in swarms without breaking fps, we can adapt our current SWARM lab in dev to also display pearl-enemies, and play with variables in how they are rendered to see where we could gain the most. overall idea: strong full resolution animations when there are few and we can appreciate them, and simplifications when they are in swarms.' What must still read in a swarm, in his order: the hop rhythm, the stalks, the colour inside; what may go first: the lumps and wobble, the contact shadow, the hull's resolution. No count target. Of the brainstorm's three approaches he chose to measure first in the lab and build the level ladder from the numbers (spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-14-swarm-lab-pearl-design.md, sections 1-5; the ladder, the per-size step rate, the solver knob, the ram in Pearl mode and a Pearl units tab are out of this round). Branch swarm-lab-pearl, cut from pearl-enemies at cdb05051.
outcome:
labs.html#swarm -> bodies: Pearl (src/labs/swarm-pearl.js, mounted by src/labs/swarm-tab.js; the dot lane unchanged, its count, density and file width shared). The bodies are the game's: createPearlFamily with PEARL_BODIES, CREATURE_FOLLOW, CREATURE_DEATH, PEARL_TIERS, PEARL_FOLLOW, PEARL_PACE, PEARL_GAIT and PEARL_IMPACT as src/fx/creature-enemies.js makes it, each record walking its paced spec speed x the sector's pace x 10 m, waiting for its body (paceOf), tracked in plane metres and freed and seated again at the far end when it reaches the tank, so the lane is always full. The lane is the canyon's (CANYON 48 x 2.4 cells, 480 x 24 m), its walls the bodies' reach; the bodies, the floor and the walls bend onto the story planet (R = 10 / STORY_SANITY.cellSide, 753 m); the game height view is the game's own tankViewPose (third person, desktop) at TANK_LENS fed the story lengths in metres (eye ~34 m up, ~29 m behind the hull), beside a free orbit. Tier picker: the eight tiers, or mix: the canyon again's swarm (sector 6 when the door is at its earliest, wave 7: drifter, gslime, amoeba, so orange, blue and white, one cored). The line: alive, step (the walk, every track() and family.step(), per frame), draw (render, gl.finish(), then a one-pixel readPixels; median of three every 0.2 s), the levels high/mid/low +culled from family.stats(), triangles, calls, the share of a 60 fps frame, each a mean over the last second. The knobs (applyKnobs; each sets only its own field; RESET to the game's: CUTIS_LOD under PEARL_FOLLOW.lod, high 70 px, low 12 px, high cap 12): high px, low px, high cap, force level, lumps (uNoise 0), breath (uBreath 0), contact shadow, inner core mesh, step every 1/2/4 frames. src/fx/cutis-maku/geometry.js reads its lod object at every update and takes lod.force (named in its header as a change from the kit; off by default); a high cap of 0 used to draw every candidate high (an index past the sorted sizes), now none. The family hands out geometries(). The sweep (100, 300, 600, 1000; settled 2 s, read 3 s, of the lab's clock) prints a table under the panel. THE FIRST SWEEP, headless Chrome on the Mac mini (kainode), white, game height, the game's knobs; headless numbers are not the owner's M4's, the deltas between two tables are the value:

```
bodies  step ms  draw ms  high/mid/low/culled  tris   calls
100     0.4      6.6      0/42/58/0            0.2M   60
300     0.9      10.5     0/146/154/0          0.5M   60
600     1.5      13.5     0/320/280/0          1.0M   60
1000    2.0      14.8     0/530/470/0          1.7M   60
```

Each knob alone, the same run (draw at 1000 bodies; run-to-run noise about 1-2 ms): lumps off 13.8, breath off 14.1, shadow off 14.1, every body forced to the mid hull 14.4 (2.7M tris), to the low hull 16.5 (0.5M tris), core mesh off 21.3 (noise; it draws fewer triangles), step every 4 frames 14.0 with the step 2.0 -> 0.7 ms; every body forced to the high hull 99 ms (28.3M tris). Read: at the game's height no white body reaches the high hull (a 2.8 m body is ~47 px at ~40 m) and none is culled in a 200 m file; the draw is not triangle-bound below the high hull (mid against low is no gain here), so the next round looks at what the draw does pay (the transparent membrane's fill and passes, the fixed cost) before the ladder. The first gl.finish-only reading was 0.1-0.3 ms from 0.2M to 28M triangles, flat: Chrome's finish did not wait for the GPU in headless, so the Pearl probe adds the readback (the dot lane's probe is unchanged and under-reads the same way). Unexplained: the step column read lower under the forced high hull (0.3-1.0 ms) than on auto.
alternatives: A ladder built blind (hero / swarm / far impostor designed from the kit's levels without numbers): the owner chose to measure first; the tables above already say the mid-to-low hull step is not where the draw goes at the game's height.
Merged cluster bodies (one membrane for several bodies in a dense swarm): the brainstorm's third approach, kept for after the measurements.

Driving the family through the game's seam (src/fx/creature-bodies.js, the hubs, the board's reach): the lab is one plane round the tank with the canyon's walls as two planes, so the seam's hubs and cell walk are left out; the family, the kit and the draw are the game's.
Reading draw with gl.finish() alone, as the dot lane does: it read flat from 0.2M to 28M triangles headless; the readback is one more wait that cannot return early.
